faq.q: I was lane splitting. Do I still have a case?
faq.a: Yes. Lane splitting is legal in California. The question is whether you were doing it reasonably — and whether the driver who hit you was paying attention. Insurers use lane splitting to scare riders out of claims. Don't let them.

You may still recover. California's comparative negligence rules mean your recovery could be reduced for injuries a helmet would have prevented — but the driver who caused the crash is still responsible for the crash. Get a free review before you assume anything.

faq.q: The insurance company already offered me money. Should I take it?
faq.a: Not before a free case review. First offers to riders are especially low because insurers assume you'll take it. Signing usually ends your claim permanently, even if your injuries get worse.

I don't have health insurance. Can I still get treated?

Nothing up front — ever. We front every cost of building your case and only collect a fee if we recover money for you. No recovery, no attorney fee.
